originality.rationale: A published all-parameter calculation of closed rook-graph neighborhoods is inapplicable to open neighborhoods. The checked full published open-neighborhood rook results cover m=n=4, or give only high-degree homology and a relative quotient for all m,n; neither gives H1=Z/2 for all m,n>=4. Exact named searches returned those as closest results, not a dominating all-parameter formula. A general fundamental-group equivalence may carry an unlocated consequence, hence residual risk.
residual_risks: Full original arXiv:1210.2803 first-version text was not retrieved (two direct PDF attempts failed); a graph-fundamental-group reduction could have an unlocated specialized consequence.
Search indexes and public records may omit equivalent statements under Hom/box-complex or graph reconfiguration terminology.
The exact first homology is established, not a complete homotopy or all-degree integral homology classification.

value.rationale: Previously known order-two homology at the finite Kummer 4-by-4 example now persists with exactly one torsion class for every pair of arbitrarily large rook factors. The result fills a concrete degree-one gap left by published general high-degree rook homology, while sharply contrasting the same family’s torsion-free closed-neighborhood sphere wedge; the universal coefficient-group proof identifies a coherent structural parity class.
